title: Your working setup
purpose: Understanding whose work these answers describe helps us avoid designing around the wrong kind of business.

questions.title: Which roles do you handle?
options: lease|Lease a vehicle or operating rights

questions.title: Whose work will your answers describe?
Which transportation services do you provide?
How many working vehicles do these answers cover?

title: How guests reach you
purpose: Knowing how guests find and contact you helps us distinguish a need for more visibility from a need for easier booking.

questions.title: How do new guests usually discover your business?
questions.help: Choose up to three. Think about how they find you, not how they send their message.

questions.title: How do booking enquiries usually reach you?
Think of a recent booking: how did it go from the first enquiry to a confirmed arrangement?
questions.help: A brief account is enough, including what worked well. Please leave out guest names and contact details.

title: What you already use
purpose: We want to understand what existing options get right, where they fall short, and why some operators choose not to use them.
note: Think of websites, listings, booking apps, marketing services or dispatch networks that help bring in or arrange work. They do not have to be paid services. If you use several, focus on one for now.

questions.title: Have you joined or used any of these services?
options: current_recent|I use one now, including within the last 30 days
current_notrecent|I use one now, but have not used it in the last 30 days
former_recent|I stopped, but used it within the last 30 days
former|I used one before, but not within the last 30 days
considered|I considered one but never joined
never|I have not considered joining one

questions.title: Which service would you like to tell us about?
questions.help: The name is optional. Please focus on the same service in the next section.

questions.title: What mainly led you to join it?
What mainly kept you from joining?
What has made your current approach sufficient so far, or left you unsure about other options?
What makes it worth continuing to use?
questions.help: If it has not proved useful yet, that is helpful to know too.

questions.title: What made you stop using it?

title: What it costs and brings back
purpose: Understanding both the cost and the return helps us judge what would make a different service worthwhile, not simply add another expense.
skipNote: Based on your earlier answer, there is no recently used service to describe here. Continue to the next section, or go back if you would like to change that answer.
note: All figures are optional. Use the same service and the last 30 days throughout. Estimates are welcome. These figures describe associated work, not proof that the service created every booking.

questions.title: How does that service charge you?
Over the last 30 days, about how much did you pay that service?
questions.help: USD. Include fees deducted before payment reached you. Enter 0 if no payment fell in this period; annual or bundled charges may make that different from the ongoing cost.

questions.title: About how many completed bookings came through that service in those 30 days?
questions.help: Count bookings, not individual passengers. Choose "Not tracked / not sure" if you cannot estimate.

questions.title: About how much guest payment did those bookings bring in, before costs and service deductions?
questions.help: USD. Exclude money belonging to other operators. This is not a profit figure.

title: The work around the driving
purpose: A booking service should reduce unnecessary work, not give you another system to look after.

questions.title: Who normally handles booking enquiries while you are driving?
options: wait|Enquiries wait until I am available

questions.title: Which non-driving tasks take the most effort?
On a typical working day, how much of your own time goes into those tasks?
What do you use to keep arrangements organised?

title: Work you could take
purpose: We need to distinguish opportunities a better process could recover from work you could not, or would not, want to take.

questions.title: In the last 30 days, about how many suitable enquiries failed to become completed work?
questions.help: Think of jobs you wanted and could reasonably have served, not work you deliberately chose to decline.

questions.title: What mainly prevented those jobs from going ahead?
What limits your ability to take additional work you would want?
When, if ever, would additional work be useful?
questions.help: A brief description is enough. "I do not want additional work" is a useful answer too.

title: What remains after expenses
purpose: More bookings only help if the extra work is worthwhile. These optional figures help us understand that distinction.
note: Use the same person, vehicle or business you described at the start, and the last 30 days. These are rough cash-flow figures, not take-home profit. Please do not send financial records or documents.

questions.title: Were the last 30 days quiet, typical or busy for your business?
Approximately how much did you collect for that work during those 30 days, before business costs or booking-service deductions?
questions.help: USD. Exclude money belonging to other operators. Include service deductions when estimating the amount before costs.

questions.title: Approximately how much did you pay in business expenses during those 30 days?
questions.help: USD. Include service costs already reported; do not add them a second time. Exclude money simply passed to other operators. Annual or unusually large payments may make this period unrepresentative.

title: What would make a difference
purpose: Your priorities help us choose what deserves building, and what must not be disrupted.

questions.title: Which improvement would make the biggest practical difference to your business?
What must a different approach preserve for you?
What have we misunderstood or not asked?
questions.help: Include anything important about your work or local arrangements that our questions missed.
